mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% over the prior 3 months reduces the risk-free rate component of equity discounting, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as valuation pressures ease.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns remain positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5% over 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 3.8% in the prior 3 months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending velocity and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 3.8%, or correlation with returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1600 thousand units and industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index level signals weakening consumer demand for goods and services, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO does not correlate with negative SPX 20d returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 300), a federal funds rate rise above 4.5% triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases real borrowing costs and reduces equity valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real sales (RSAFS) above 680,000 million dollars over the prior 3 months signals robust consumer spending that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS trend does not correlate with positive SPX 20d returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) fall below 155,000 thousand in the prior 3 months, it indicates labor market contraction that reduces household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 155000, or correlation with returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A relative increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding CPIAUCSL inflation rate by > 0.5 percentage points over the prior 3 months signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases real interest rates and reduces equity risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The FEDFUNDS-CPIAUCSL spread does not predict negative SPX 60d returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 3.0% annually), a housing starts (HOUST) decline below 1600 thousand units signals sector-specific cooling that reduces consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth rate > 3.0% AND HOUST < 1600
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and HOUST < 1600, or Rank IC < 0.03.
